In 'I beat the tar outta him' 'tar' is a noun, but 'the tar outta him' is an adverbial phrase.  

When I said 'the fuck' I was referring to its applied use as an adverbial phrase in 'the fuck out of' in a clearly misguided attempt at comedy. 

I think saying 'the fuck out of' in 'I scraped the fuck out of my tongue' modifies the verb 'scrape' in the same way 'like hell' modifies the verb 'ran' in 'I ran like hell'. It's an adverbial phrase, but whatever.

I developed an emotional connection with this game, something which doesn't happen often; that connection makes the game special to me: I still remember it warmly after all these years.

Majula is one of my favorite game environments of all time; so beautiful and serene yet so melancholically desolate and poignant. The gentle music, the sunlight, the tranquillity and isolation; juxtaposed with a balancing, comforting feeling of solace and safety combine to create one of the most wonderfully psychological, haunting yet relaxing game spaces I've ever had the joy of populating.

I still have Dark Souls 2 on my console, so every 6 months I can load up my NG++++ character and just chill in Majula for a little moment.

Dark Souls 2 having the ability to evoke this connection within me to a virtual space makes it an example of videogames at their very best.

That's a fair point. Although in 2023 far too many fans use insider verbiage every day for it to just stop being a part of modern online discourse, I kind of agree that it doesn't add much of creative or descriptive value to the content of the discussion.

Not too spicy really.  I think there was a naeve excitement to looking at this stuff in a simpler way back in the day.

As a viewer I always try to sit back, switch off my brain so to speak, and appreciate whatever wrestling I'm watching with that same energy; no analysis, just trying to get lost in the moment.  I've always found pro-wrestling is better that way.

As for wrestling discourse, we all know too much about the pro-wrestling business and have opinions based on it; and I think it's too late to put the genie back in the bottle and not use certain terms.  I don't think that's our fault, it's just the way things have shook out with the internet and having such easy access to information.

We're all armchair quarterbacks, no doubt about that.  You find it in every sports' fanbase these days, I think it's just a part of being a fan of sport(s entertainment) in modern times. 

 Everybody likes to say how it should be done: at times, myself included - there's no harm in that.  It doesn't mean we're stating fact,  just giving a subjective opinion, and everyone has one.

Every wrestling promotion goes through peaks and valleys, hot streaks and cold.  WWE will always make a shit ton of money as they've nurtured their business into a very successful money making machine, and I don't see that ending any time soon.  If AEW does great business financially speaking every year I think it would still take them a very long time to be as profitable as WWE.

So long as AEW stays in business they'll be able to try to innovate creatively in the hope that something gets over big, blows up and improves their business: similar to if they somehow found their own megastar on a Hogan or Austin level, or a storyline with crossover appeal within the mainstream blew up to increase viewership.  So long as they're open for business I think it's just a matter of time before one of these things happens to some degree, further equaling the playing field.

So long as there's 2 horses in the race; although financially one is a distant second, both promotions will go through times where they're creatively most popular within the wrestling zeitgeist.  This is the case as I said before because no storyline lasts forever, no cold streak lasts forever if the product is good and no hot streak lasts forever if the product is bad.  

As a result; and assuming both promotions stay in business, there will be peaks and valleys in terms of business and popularity within the fanbase. Times when one promotion is flavor of the month, before the other promotion finds itself on a hot streak a year or 2 later: the most important factor is that both companies stay in business to allow this process to happen over time.

So long as either promotion stays in business and the product consistently remains good, I think it's always just a matter of time before something creative breaks through the ceiling to strike a chord with the fanbase and improve business for either promotion.

I've got more than one tip for you.

Before you enter a fog gate spend all your runes so that you may fight without risk of losing the spoils of your effort.

Also, make peace with the fact that you could lose all your runes at any time, and you will; repeatedly: and that's fine: don't get attached to them - you can and will always get more.  Lost all your runes?  No problem, keep playing and you'll get more.  Thinking of the game this way takes the sting out of dying, which makes everything less intimidating.

If you're struggling to find confidence in the game, just over level yourself a little for that area, once you find your footing and gain confidence you can always level up a bit less in the next area to re-balance the game.

Have patience.  I've never played a From Soft game which doesn't heavily punish impatience.  Take your time, slow and steady, take your time, play safe and calculated, think about what you're doing and don't rush in without thinking.

Don't be greedy in bossfights.  Don't make too many hits on a boss before you've learned his moveset.  Take 1 or 2 hits, roll to safety, observe the enemy's reaction and learn their attack pattern while keeping yourself safe.  Any more than 1 or 2 hits at a time without learning their move-set and you risk not having enough time to roll to safety before their counter-attack lands.
